newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Merrill Lynch analyst sees coffee prices firm.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch analyst sees coffee prices firm.

text.p: Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said low consumer inventories and weak production forecasts should provide near-term support for relatively high coffee prices.
Ganes, who spoke at a meeting on the outlook for Colombia's coffee industry, said she sees coffee selling on world markets at about $1.40 to $1.50 a lb by mid-year.
Although she said she doubted the recent runup in prices would extend into next year, she stressed that low consumer stockpiles provided a favorable outlook for producer countries overall.

In her remarks, Ganes also said Colombia's output during the 1996-97 coffee year should total anywhere between 9.3 and 10.2 million 60-kg bags. Both figures are below the 10.4 million bag estimate of National Coffee Growers' Federation.

Noting one possible drawback to the recent rise in world prices, Ganes said a growing number of U.S. roasters were steering away from premium arabica coffees, or using less of them in their blends, in favor of less pricey robustas.
"The roasters are moving away from arabica and prefer robusta whenever possible," she said.
